title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttnV2 + fused ops + improved ROPE handling
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: This PR upgrades the attention execution path in the serving runtime to use a patched FlashAttention V2 kernel, fuses rotary/ROPE application into the attention kernel where safe, and adds heuristics to the scheduling layer to prefer fused kernels and KV-aware batching. Motivation: reduce per-token latency and GPU kernel-launch overhead on long-context and streaming workloads while preserving numeric stability across model variants. Summary of changes: - Add FlashAttnV2 backend + fallbacks for older CUDA versions. - Implement fused ROPE/rotary application inside kernel for models that use rotary embeddings; fall back to existing path for models with nonstandard ROPE placement. - Introduce a fused QKV packing path to reduce memory traffic when running FP16/INT8 quantized variants. - KV-batching modifications: scheduler detects high KV reuse patterns and groups requests to maintain KV cache locality, reducing CUDA memory thrash. - Scheduling: new kernel selector heuristics (sequence length, kv-cache hit ratio, batch size) and a runtime flag to force fused kernels for canary testing. - Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for latency, throughput, and memory usage; end-to-end regression suites to validate output fidelity. Checklist:
- [x] Add FlashAttnV2 integration and kernel selection logic
- [x] Fuse ROPE/rotary ops when safe
- [x] Update scheduler heuristics and KV-batching rules
- [x] Add microbenchmarks and perf dashboards
- [x] Add gated config and rollout plan for Dedicated/Private slices
Commits (high-level): - feat(attn): integrate flashattn v2 kernels and registration hooks - perf(attn): fuse rotary/ROPE ops into attention kernel, add safe-guards - perf(kv): schedule KV-aware batching and locality heuristics - perf(scheduler): kernel selector improvements + runtime flags - test(perf): add microbench harness and per-kernel telemetry

release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels: integrate FlashAttentionV2 with fused ROPE/rotary ops and KV-aware batching. Improves p50 latency by ~15-28% and throughput by up to 22% in common workloads. Rollout is gated; disabled by default for Private installer.
safety_notes: Fallbacks added for models with nonstandard ROPE placement; numeric regression tests added. Gate enabled to disable for sensitive production slices.
backout_plan: If regressions observed, set runtime.feature.attn_fused_kernels=false and revert kernel-selector rollout; rollback steps documented in deploy/rollout/gates/attn_fused_kernels.yaml
